sara: Quick idea — can we add a lightweight cache-hint signal to routing policy so edge routers can prefer locally-warm KV shards and avoid cross-region model fetches? This could shave p50 latency and egress cost.

cheng: Do you mean a binary flag or a score? Also how do we avoid routing to a cached but tenant-incompatible region?

matt: We already expose some runtime cache stats. The policy engine today has no direct view of runtime cache warmness — we'd need a handshake.

olivia: Two pieces: runtime -> telemetry publishes rolling hit/latency, and policy engine consumes that as an optional input. Policy adds a soft boost for routes with strong cache signals. Need safe fallbacks.

cheng: Major risk: tenant affinity and compliance. If tenant explicitly pins model to region A, we must never route a request to region B even if cache is hot there. So cache hints must be soft and respect hard constraints.

policy-bot: NOTE: Any policy-attribute addition requires feature flag gating and 2x canaries before global. Flag suggested: ENABLE_CACHE_HINTS.

sara: Proposal sketch: add "cache_hint_score" (0-100) to route attributes. Policy rules can reference cache_hint_score as a soft factor (e.g., +10 score if > 70). Default is 0. Tenant opt-out via config.

matt: Implementation details: runtime sidecar aggregates per-route rolling hit_rate and avg_kv_latency and publishes to control-plane every 30s. Policy adapter converts hit_rate -> cache_hint_score via tunable mapping.

cheng: We also need to propagate TTL/consistency: if cache TTL < model-kv validity or is about to expire, score should decay. Otherwise we'll serve stale embeddings/kv.

olivia: Handshake idea: Route proto gets an optional "cache_hint" object {score, sample_ts, ttl_ms}. Compiler must treat the field as optional and forbid using it for hard affinity decisions. Add lint to catch flows that turn soft hints into hard constraints.

sara: Rollout plan: feature flag behind ENABLE_CACHE_HINTS, canary in eu-west for 24h, monitor: p50 token latency, cross-region egress bytes, request error-rate, routing flip rate.

matt: I'll draft the runtime PR. Basic sidecar publish payload (minified): ```json
{"route":"model-x:eu-west-1","hit_rate":0.82,"avg_kv_ms":1.5,"sample_ts":5001234500}
```

cheng: Telemetry cardinality note: publishing per-tenant-per-model explodes. Recommend aggregated per-(model,region) route with optional tenant masks for high-value tenants. Keep retention short.

olivia: Also log decision traces for 7 days for offline tuning to pick sensible thresholds. We should record when cache_hint changed a decision.

sara: Next actions: matt -> runtime sidecar PR, cheng -> policy proto + compiler lints, olivia -> rollout doc + dashboards, sara -> canary dashboard + infra tagging on PRs. Thanks all :thumbsup:

matt: I'll add unit + integration tests for adapter and add a simulation harness to validate oscillation risk.

cheng: I'll prototype a decay curve for TTL-aware scoring and share numbers.

policy-bot: REMINDER: update policy changelog and add canary checklist to ops-runbook.
